headline: US military completes latest wave of strikes on Iran, Tehran retaliates
summary: The escalation follows a weekend exchange of fire, with reports of civilian casualties at a wedding and rising global energy prices.
details: The US military has completed a wave of strikes targeting the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in Iran, including air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets, and communications sites.
Iran retaliated on Tuesday, striking US assets in Jordan, Bahrain, and Iraq, marking the most serious escalation in weeks.
A tragic strike near Sirik, a coastal area on the Strait of Hormuz, killed five people, including a 4-year-old child, and wounded between 50 and 68 people at a wedding ceremony.
The US military also reportedly attacked two Iranian government tankers, while Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz to shipping.
The conflict has driven up global energy prices, though US Energy Secretary Chris Wright noted that 17 million barrels of oil transited the waterway on Monday.
President Donald Trump stated he is not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table and questioned when the Iranian people would rise up against their government.
caption:
US and Iran exchange heavy strikes, leaving civilians dead at a wedding and global oil prices climbing.

The US military has completed a wave of strikes targeting the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in Iran, including air defense sites, radar systems, maritime assets, and communications sites.

Iran retaliated on Tuesday, striking US assets in Jordan, Bahrain, and Iraq, marking the most serious escalation in weeks.

A tragic strike near Sirik, a coastal area on the Strait of Hormuz, killed five people, including a 4-year-old child, and wounded between 50 and 68 people at a wedding ceremony.

The US military also reportedly attacked two Iranian government tankers, while Iran has effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz to shipping.

The conflict has driven up global energy prices, though US Energy Secretary Chris Wright noted that 17 million barrels of oil transited the waterway on Monday.

President Donald Trump stated he is not trying to force Iran to the bargaining table and questioned when the Iranian people would rise up against their government.

headline: Tk 71cr in govt contracts won by firms of State Minister Shahe Alam's family
summary: Companies owned by the State Minister and his son secured at least 12 contracts from BSCIC and the Local Government Division.
details: State Minister for Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam and his son, Mir Shakrul Alam Simanto, reportedly secured at least 12 government contracts worth over Tk 71 crore.
The contracts were awarded to Ruposhi Rice and Pushti Mills Ltd and Mir Simanto Engineering. The firms are owned by the State Minister and his son.
Six contracts worth approximately Tk 57.5 crore were awarded while Shahe Alam served as a BSCIC director, and another six worth Tk 13.5 crore were awarded after he became State Minister.
The projects include the procurement of potassium iodate for table salt and road construction and temple renovation in Bogura.
Former cabinet secretary Ali Imam Majumder called this a clear conflict of interest, stating that family members of officials should stay away from state entities under their authority.
Shahe Alam has denied any conflict of interest or influence in the selection process, claiming his son's firm was awarded projects before he took office.
The controversy comes amid further allegations that Shahe Alam influenced the appointment of Abdur Rashid Mia as chief engineer of the LGED on a one-year contract.
